title: OpenAI Asks Judge to Dismiss Apple's Trade Secrets Lawsuit
excerpt: OpenAI has asked a federal judge to dismiss Apple's lawsuit accusing the AI company of stealing trade secrets, calling the allegations...
content_html:
OpenAI has asked a federal judge to dismiss Apple's lawsuit accusing the AI company of stealing trade secrets, calling the allegations "meritless."


Lawyers for OpenAI said Apple's suit twists the actions of its employees. Bloomberg reports that the filing defends Chief Hardware Officer Tang Yew Tan, who spent 24 years at Apple as VP of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch before leaving to co-found io Products with former Apple design chief Jony Ive. io merged with OpenAI in July 2025. OpenAI said Tan followed normal industry recruiting practices when interviewing Apple staff.

OpenAI also defended senior systems engineer Chang Liu, one of two former Apple employees named in the suit. Apple claims Liu accessed confidential hardware files over several weeks after finding an authentication bug. OpenAI said Liu was simply helping a former Apple colleague find information for their own work, and published excerpts of text messages it says back up that account. "Apple should not be permitted to use a baseless and pretextual lawsuit," OpenAI's lawyers wrote.

OpenAI's motion argues Apple never properly identified what information actually counts as a protectable trade secret. The company said it has no interest in Apple's confidential material because it is "building something entirely new and different from anything at Apple."

Axios reported that OpenAI's filing also disputes how Apple built its case. According to OpenAI, Apple's own security practices, including letting staff use personal iCloud accounts for work and later reviewing personal messages left on company devices, are what gave former employees leftover system access in the first place, not evidence of a coordinated theft. The 31 page filing repeatedly frames the case as Apple trying to cover for its own struggles, with variations of the word "fail" appearing nearly 50 times.

OpenAI's filing also revisited an earlier dispute over how the two sides first fell out of contact. Apple's suit had claimed OpenAI never responded to its outreach in February, and that the two sides discussed the matter with OpenAI's general counsel. OpenAI says neither is true, and that the breakdown traced back to Apple's own outside counsel confusing two OpenAI employees with similar surnames and sending a message to the wrong person.

This week's motion follows the suit Apple filed against OpenAI in July, which accuses the company of running a scheme to pull confidential product information out of job candidates and new hires. Apple and OpenAI had spent about two years partnering to build ChatGPT integration into Siri, but the relationship soured as OpenAI moved into hardware, a shift accelerated by its acquisition of Ive's startup. Apple's suit claims more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI.

Apple escalated the case further this week, asking the same judge for a preliminary injunction to stop OpenAI from using any alleged trade secrets while the case continues, along with expedited discovery targeting Liu, Tan, OpenAI and its foundation, and io. Apple said its investigation has since turned up 11 more former employees who may have been witnesses or otherwise involved, beyond Liu, Tan, and previously named OpenAI employee Yu-Ting Peng.

Apple claims one former employee met with Liu and Peng before Peng's OpenAI interview and discussed proprietary information about unannounced products, and that another took screenshots of confidential documents relating to an unannounced Apple product before their own interview. Apple also said that after it filed its complaint, several former staffers now at OpenAI reached out about returning Apple issued devices they had kept.

OpenAI called that injunction request "based on false information and completely unnecessary" in a public blog post responding to Apple's filing. OpenAI has a court ordered deadline of August 17 to formally respond to Apple's preliminary injunction request. The judge is set to hear arguments on October 1.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 已要求联邦法官驳回苹果公司指控这家人工智能公司窃取商业机密的诉讼，称这些指控“毫无根据”。

OpenAI 的律师表示，苹果的诉讼扭曲了其员工的行为。 彭博社报道称，该文件为首席硬件官 Tang Yew Tan 进行了辩护，Tang Yew Tan 在苹果公司工作了 24 年，担任 iPhone 和 Apple Watch 产品设计副总裁，之后与苹果前设计总监 Jony Ive 共同创立了 io Products。 io 于 2025 年 7 月与 OpenAI 合并。 OpenAI 表示，Tan 在面试苹果员工时遵循了正常的行业招聘惯例。

OpenAI 还为高级系统工程师刘畅（Chang Liu）辩护，刘畅是诉讼中提到的两名前苹果员工之一。 苹果声称刘在发现身份验证错误后几周内访问了机密硬件文件。 OpenAI 表示，刘只是帮助一位前苹果同事查找自己工作所需的信息，并发布了据称支持该帐户的短信摘录。 OpenAI 的律师写道：“不应允许苹果公司提起毫无根据和借口的诉讼。”

OpenAI 的动议认为，苹果从未正确确定哪些信息实际上算作受保护的商业秘密。 该公司表示，它对苹果公司的机密材料没有兴趣，因为它正在“打造全新的、与苹果公司不同的东西”。

Axios 报道称，OpenAI 的文件还对苹果如何立案提出了争议。 据 OpenAI 称，苹果公司自身的安全实践，包括让员工使用个人 iCloud 帐户进行工作，以及随后审查公司设备上留下的个人消息，才是让前员工获得剩余系统访问权限的首要原因，而不是协同盗窃的证据。 这份长达 31 页的文件反复将这一案件描述为苹果试图掩盖自己的困境，其中“失败”一词的变体出现了近 50 次。

OpenAI 的文件还重新审视了早些时候关于双方最初如何失去联系的争议。 苹果公司的诉讼称，OpenAI 从未对其 2 月份的外展做出回应，双方与 OpenAI 的总法律顾问讨论了此事。 OpenAI 表示这两者都不是真的，并且故障可以追溯到苹果自己的外部法律顾问混淆了两名姓氏相似的 OpenAI 员工并向错误的人发送了消息。

本周的动议是在苹果公司于 7 月份对 OpenAI 提起诉讼之后提出的，该诉讼指控该公司实施一项计划，从求职者和新员工那里获取机密产品信息。 苹果和 OpenAI 花了大约两年的时间合作将 ChatGPT 集成到 Siri 中，但随着 OpenAI 进军硬件领域，这种关系恶化了，收购 Ive 的初创公司加速了这一转变。 苹果公司的诉讼称，目前有超过 400 名前苹果员工在 OpenAI 工作。

苹果公司本周进一步升级了案件，要求同一法官发布初步禁令，在案件继续进行期间阻止 OpenAI 使用任何所谓的商业秘密，并加快针对 Liu、Tan、OpenAI 及其基金会和 io 的调查。 苹果表示，除刘、谭和此前名为 OpenAI 的员工 Yu-Ting Peng 之外，调查还发现了另外 11 名前员工，他们可能是证人或以其他方式参与其中。

苹果声称，一名前员工在彭接受 OpenAI 采访之前会见了刘和彭，并讨论了有关未发布产品的专有信息，而另一名前员工在接受采访之前截取了与未发布苹果产品相关的机密文件的屏幕截图。 苹果还表示，在提出投诉后，OpenAI 的几名前员工主动联系，要求归还他们保留的苹果发行的设备。

OpenAI 在回应苹果申请的公开博客文章中称该禁令请求“基于虚假信息，完全没有必要”。 法院命令 OpenAI 在 8 月 17 日之前正式回应苹果的初步禁令请求。 法官定于 10 月 1 日听取辩论。
